description: Building a working compiler for a small language, phase by phase: lexing, parsing, syntax trees, semantic analysis, intermediate code, optimisation and code generation for a real or virtual machine. Taught to the depth of a leading compilers course.
modelledOn: Aho, Lam, Sethi and Ullman, Compilers: Principles, Techniques, and Tools
Appel, Modern Compiler Implementation in Java/C/ML
Cooper and Torczon, Engineering a Compiler
outcomes: Specify tokens with regular expressions and build a lexer by hand and with a generator.
Write grammars, eliminate ambiguity and left recursion, and build recursive-descent, LL(1) and LR parsers.
Construct abstract syntax trees and perform semantic analysis with symbol tables and type checking.
Translate to intermediate representations such as three-address code and SSA.
Apply local and global optimisations driven by dataflow analysis.
Generate code with instruction selection, register allocation and runtime support, and test the compiler end to end.

units.title: Overview of compilation
topics: Compilers, interpreters, JIT compilers and transpilers; the phases and their data structures
The source language for the course (a small C-like or Pascal-like language) and the target (RISC-V, x86 or a VM)
Bootstrapping, cross-compilation, the toolchain (assembler, linker, loader)
Project setup: test suite, driver, error reporting conventions

units.title: Lexical analysis
topics: Tokens, lexemes, patterns; keywords, identifiers, literals, comments, whitespace
Regular expressions to NFA (Thompson), NFA to DFA (subset construction), DFA minimisation
Hand-written scanners versus generators (lex/flex, ANTLR); longest match and lookahead
Error recovery in the lexer; Unicode and source positions for error messages

units.title: Parsing: top-down
topics: Context-free grammars, derivations, parse trees, ambiguity; precedence and associativity in grammars
Eliminating left recursion and left factoring; FIRST and FOLLOW sets
Recursive-descent parsing; predictive LL(1) table-driven parsing
Error recovery: panic mode, synchronising tokens; good error messages
Pratt parsing for expressions

units.title: Parsing: bottom-up
topics: Shift-reduce parsing, handles, conflicts
LR(0) items and automaton, SLR, LR(1), LALR(1) table construction
Parser generators (yacc/bison, ANTLR); resolving conflicts with precedence declarations
Comparing LL and LR; generalised and PEG parsing in brief

units.title: Abstract syntax trees
topics: Concrete versus abstract syntax; designing AST node classes
Building the AST during parsing; semantic actions and syntax-directed translation
Tree traversal with the visitor pattern; pretty printing and AST dumps for debugging
Attribute grammars: synthesised and inherited attributes

units.title: Semantic analysis and symbol tables
topics: Scopes, declarations, name resolution; symbol table design with nested scopes
Type systems: type expressions, equivalence, coercion, overloading; type checking expressions, statements and functions
Semantic checks: declared before use, break inside loop, return paths, constant expressions
Type inference in brief; error reporting and recovery

units.title: Intermediate code and runtime environments
topics: Three-address code, quadruples, control-flow graphs; translating expressions, control flow (short-circuit booleans), arrays and records
Static single assignment form and its construction
Runtime organisation: activation records, calling conventions, stack frames, parameter passing, nested functions
Heap management and garbage collection basics; exceptions

units.title: Optimisation
topics: Local optimisations: constant folding, algebraic simplification, common subexpression elimination, copy propagation, dead code
Dataflow analysis: reaching definitions, live variables, available expressions; the iterative framework
Global optimisations: global CSE, loop-invariant code motion, strength reduction, induction variables
Peephole optimisation; inlining; introduction to LLVM passes

units.title: Code generation
topics: Instruction selection: tree pattern matching, simple macro expansion
Register allocation: liveness, interference graphs, graph colouring, spilling; linear scan
Instruction scheduling and target-specific details; generating assembly and linking with a runtime
End-to-end: compiling and running test programs; performance comparison against a reference compiler

schedule.title: Compilers, phases and project setup
schedule.exercise: Draw the phase diagram of a compiler for a small C-like language, naming the data structure passed between each pair of phases, and write the project test plan.

tasks.title: Step a tiny expression through lexing, parsing and code generation in the visualiser and record the data structure produced after each phase
Write a driver script that runs a toolchain of lexer, compiler stub, assembler and linker on a hello program and reports which stage failed on a broken input
Build a test harness with 12 source programs and expected outputs, run it against a stub compiler and report pass and fail counts with positioned error messages

schedule.title: Regular expressions, NFAs and DFAs
schedule.exercise: Prove by construction that a given regular expression for cedi amounts matches exactly the intended strings, with a Thompson NFA and a subset-construction table.

tasks.title: Write regular expressions for identifiers, integers, decimals and comments and test each against 20 accepted and 20 rejected strings
Convert the regular expression (a|b)*abb to an NFA with Thompson construction, then to a DFA by subset construction, and trace the input babb
Minimise a given 9-state DFA by partition refinement and verify the minimal automaton accepts the same 30 test strings

schedule.title: Building scanners
schedule.exercise: Compare a hand-written scanner and a generated one on the same token set in a short report covering speed, readability and error handling.

tasks.title: Write a hand-coded scanner for a small language that returns token type, lexeme and line number, using longest match for operators like <= and ==
Extend the scanner with a table-driven DFA for numbers and identifiers and prove equal output on 15 given programs
Make the scanner recover from illegal characters and unterminated strings, reporting line and column and continuing so one run lists every lexical error

schedule.title: Grammars and LL(1) parsing
schedule.exercise: Rewrite an ambiguous expression grammar into an unambiguous LL(1) grammar and show the FIRST and FOLLOW tables and a parse of two sample inputs.

tasks.title: Show two different parse trees for 1 + 2 * 3 under an ambiguous grammar, then fix the grammar so precedence and left associativity hold
Eliminate left recursion from an expression grammar, then compute its FIRST and FOLLOW sets and fill the LL(1) parse table
Write a recursive-descent parser for statements with if, while and assignments and verify it accepts 10 valid programs and rejects 10 invalid ones

schedule.title: Error recovery and Pratt parsing
schedule.exercise: Take five programs with typical student errors and write the single error message you would want the compiler to print for each, justifying the wording.

tasks.title: Add panic-mode recovery with synchronising tokens to a recursive-descent parser and confirm it reports three separate syntax errors in one file
Implement a Pratt parser for expressions with binding powers and test precedence of unary minus, exponent and ternary operators on 15 inputs
Add right-associative operators and a function-call postfix operator to the Pratt parser and compare its parse trees against a given reference

schedule.title: Shift-reduce and LR parsing
schedule.exercise: Build the LR(0) item sets by hand for a five-production grammar and explain where the first conflict appears and why.

tasks.title: Trace a shift-reduce parse of id + id * id on a given stack table, marking each handle and the action taken at every step
Construct the LR(0) automaton and the SLR table for a small grammar and parse two strings using the table
Show that a given grammar is SLR-conflicted but LALR(1) clean by building the LR(1) lookaheads, and list the merged states

schedule.title: Parser generators and parsing strategies
schedule.exercise: Write a short comparison table of LL, LR, PEG and generalised parsing for three kinds of language feature, and recommend one for the course language.

tasks.title: Write a yacc-style grammar for a calculator, resolve its shift-reduce conflicts with precedence declarations and test 15 expressions
Implement a small PEG parser with ordered choice for arithmetic and show a case where PEG and CFG readings of the same grammar differ
Diagnose and fix the conflicts reported for a faulty dangling-else grammar, and justify the chosen resolution with parse traces of three programs

schedule.title: Abstract syntax trees and attributes
schedule.exercise: Design the AST node classes for the course language on paper, then argue which information belongs in the AST and which was dropped from the parse tree.

tasks.title: Define AST node classes for expressions, assignments and if statements and print the tree for five source snippets using a pretty-printer
Write a visitor that evaluates constant expressions on the AST and another that counts nodes by type, and check results on 10 programs
Compute synthesised and inherited attributes for a binary-number grammar on a given parse tree and show the dependency graph and evaluation order

schedule.title: Symbol tables and type checking
schedule.exercise: Write the typing rules in inference-rule form for assignment, addition and function calls in the course language and test them on examples.

tasks.title: Implement a symbol table with nested scopes, then resolve every identifier in three programs and report undeclared uses with line numbers
Write a type checker for expressions with int, float and bool, including implicit int to float coercion, and check 15 programs with expected errors
Add semantic checks for break outside loops, missing return paths and duplicate declarations, and verify the compiler finds all seeded errors in a faulty program

schedule.title: Intermediate code and runtime environments
schedule.exercise: Translate a loop with a short-circuit condition into three-address code by hand, draw its control-flow graph and the stack frame for a recursive call.

tasks.title: Generate three-address code for arithmetic expressions and if-else statements and print the quadruples for five programs
Convert a given control-flow graph with a loop into SSA form by placing phi functions at dominance frontiers and rename the variables
Trace the stack and frame pointers through a recursive factorial call with a nested function, drawing each activation record and returning the correct value

schedule.title: Local optimisation and dataflow analysis
schedule.exercise: Optimise a short basic block by hand with constant folding, copy propagation and dead code removal, listing each step and justifying its safety.

tasks.title: Implement constant folding and algebraic simplification passes on three-address code and show before and after listings for five blocks
Run reaching definitions iteratively on a given six-block flow graph, listing the in and out sets in every round until a fixed point
Implement live-variable analysis and use it to eliminate dead stores from three-address code, verifying program output stays equal on 10 inputs

schedule.title: Global optimisation and LLVM
schedule.exercise: Pick a nested loop from a numerical routine and describe, with code, which global optimisations apply and what each saves.

tasks.title: Move a loop-invariant computation out of a loop in three-address code by hand and count how many instructions execute before and after
Implement strength reduction of i * 4 to an additive induction variable on a loop and confirm identical results on 10 inputs
Compare unoptimised and optimised output of a real compiler on a small function, identify four applied passes and relate each to a taught technique

schedule.title: Code generation and end-to-end compiler
schedule.exercise: Write a one-page evaluation of the finished compiler comparing generated code size and speed against a reference compiler on five programs.

tasks.title: Generate stack-machine or register assembly for arithmetic expressions by tree pattern matching and run the output on a simulator for 10 inputs
Build the interference graph for a given live-range table, colour it with three registers and spill one variable where necessary
Compile and run 12 test programs through the full pipeline, compare outputs and run time against a reference compiler, and report three failures with causes
